skill.displayName: 波龙股神量化交易系统

vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: bowlong-quant-aio
Version: 2.1.1

The bundle is a comprehensive and well-documented quantitative trading system ('波龙股神') for A-shares and futures. It contains functional modules for multi-factor stock selection, backtesting with market-specific rules (T+1, price limits), and trade execution via Huaxin QMT and Wenhua WH8 APIs. While the system handles sensitive credentials like API tokens and trading account info, the code (specifically in `executor_huaxin.py`, `executor_wenhua.py`, and `risk_monitor.py`) uses them strictly for intended purposes, such as communicating with local trading servers or the official Telegram API for alerts. No evidence of data exfiltration, malicious obfuscation, or prompt injection was found.

llm.summary: The skill appears to implement the described quant/real‑money trading features, but the declared requirements underreport the sensitive credentials and runtime bindings the SKILL.md and code actually use — review before providing any real account credentials or enabling live trading.

dimensions.detail: Name, description and included scripts (stock picker, backtester, risk monitor, QMT/WH8 executors) align with a quant trading workstation: python3 + market-data token(s) + optional broker APIs are expected for this purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md instructs the agent to read and edit config files and to run scripts that access market data and broker APIs. It also references several environment variables and local services (QMT, WH8, TBQuant3, Telegram push) beyond the single env var declared in the registry metadata. The scripts will read config/config.yaml and other config files and can invoke trading executors that send orders (to local broker HTTP APIs or COM interfaces).
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec is provided (instruction-only); the package contains Python scripts and config files that will be present on disk. No remote downloads or package installs are performed by the skill itself, so install risk is limited to the provided code bundle (which you should still review).
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Registry metadata only lists TUSHARE_TOKEN as required, but SKILL.md and config files reference multiple additional sensitive environment variables (QMT_ACCOUNT, QMT_PASSWORD, WH8_ACCOUNT/WH8_PASSWORD, TB_ACCOUNT, PUSH_TOKEN, PUSH_CHAT_ID, etc.). The code will use those credentials for real trading if provided. Declaring only TUSHARE_TOKEN is inconsistent and understates credential scope.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always:false and standard autonomous invocation settings. The skill does not request permanent system‑wide privileges in metadata and does not attempt to modify other skills; however, when given broker credentials and when connected to the broker/local API, it can place trades — a high-impact capability that requires caution.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill contains full trading code (backtest, stock picker, risk monitor and executors for Huaxin QMT and Wenhua WH8). Before installing or running: 1) Note the registry only declared TUSHARE_TOKEN but the SKILL.md and config reference many other sensitive env vars (broker account/passwords, push tokens). Do not supply real broker credentials until you have audited the executor code and tested in paper mode. 2) Confirm the endpoints: executors default to localhost (127.0.0.1) ports for broker services — verify they do not point to remote servers in your configuration. 3) Run first in an isolated/test environment and set executor.mode/paper to avoid live orders. 4) If you plan to use live trading, review the executor_* scripts line-by-line (they implement order/HTTP/COM calls) and verify handling of credentials, error paths, and logging. 5) Prefer cloning the upstream GitHub repo, checking commit history and signatures, and running static analysis before giving any secrets to the skill.
